page: Microsoft Azure D96a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7452 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes dedicated CPU allocation with 2.0 threads per core. Memory capacity is 384.0 GB, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 2458 GB of local SSD storage, while offering zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core stress-ng performance is positioned in the bottom 10%, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores fall in the middle 50%. However, multi-threaded workloads perform significantly better, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, PassMark CPU score, and software compilation with Clang all ranking in the top 25%. Cryptographic performance is particularly strong, with the PassMark CPU encryption test reaching the top 10%, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA_NI instruction sets. Memory performance is also robust, showing top 25% results in cached small-block read bandwidth and PassMark memory scores, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidths remain in the middle 50%.

Given its hardware profile, the D96a_v4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that can leverage its 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384 GB of RAM without requiring high single-core clock speeds. It is well-suited for multi-threaded software compilation, cryptographic processing, database operations, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks, such as text generation using 7B models where it achieves top 25% performance. The integrated 2458 GB local SSD storage further supports data-intensive operations, though the lack of GPU acceleration limits its utility for heavy deep learning training.
